# Machine Learning foR Psychologists

[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20Educational%20Resources-Compatable-brightgreen)](https://creativecommons.org/about/program-areas/education-oer/)
[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/CC-BY--NC%204.0-lightgray)](http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/)
[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/Language-R-blue)](http://cran.r-project.org/)
[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/Language-Python-blue)](http://python.org/)

<sub>*Last updated `r Sys.Date()`.*</sub>

This Github repo contains all lesson files for *Machine Learning in R and Python*.
The goal is to impart students with the basic tools to construct, evaluate and compare various **machine learning models, using [`tidymodels`](https://www.tidymodels.org/) and [`scikit-learn`](https://scikit-learn.org/)**,
based on [_An Introduction to Statistical Learning_](https://www.statlearning.com/).

These topics are taught in the graduate-level course ***Machine Learning for Psychologists*** (Psych Dep., Ben-Gurion University of the Negev; Psych Dep., Tel-Aviv University). This course assumes basic competence in R and Python (importing, regression modeling, plotting, etc.).[^rprev]

[^rprev]: For R, this mean something along the lines of [*Practical Applications in R for Psychologists*](https://github.com/mattansb/Practical-Applications-in-R-for-Psychologists).


**Notes:**

- This repo contains only materials relating to *Practical Applications in R*, and does not contain any theoretical or introductory materials.
- Please note that some code does not work *on purpose*, to force students to learn to debug.

## Setup

You will need:

1. A fresh installation of [**`R`**](https://cran.r-project.org/) (preferably 4.5.0+) and [**`Python`**](https://www.python.org/) (preferably 3.13+).
2. [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/download)[^rstudio].
3. The following packages and modules:

[^rstudio]: It is also possible to use [RStudio](https://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/), but Positron is preferred.

### R Packages

```{r}
script_deps <- function(fl, comment = FALSE) {
  txt <- read.delim(fl, header = FALSE)[[1]] |>
    stringr::str_trim()

  if (isFALSE(comment)) {
    # remove comments from the code
    txt <- stringr::str_remove_all(txt, pattern = "(?<=#).*")
  }
  txt <- stringr::str_remove_all(txt, pattern = "(?<=pak::pak).*")

  pkgs <- stringr::str_extract_all(
    string = txt,
    pattern = "((?<=(library|require)\\()[a-zA-Z0-9\\.]{1,}(?=(\\)|,))|[a-zA-Z0-9\\.]{1,}(?=\\:{2}))",
    simplify = TRUE
  )

  unique(pkgs[nzchar(pkgs)])
}

pkgs <- tibble(
  script = list.files(pattern = ".R$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE),
  Lesson = dirname(script) |> str_remove("^\\./"),
  Packages = map(script, script_deps, comment = TRUE)
)

pkgs_info <- unlist(pkgs$Packages) |>
  unique() |>
  setdiff(tidyverse::tidyverse_packages()) |>
  setdiff(tidymodels::tidymodels_packages()) |>
  setdiff(easystats::easystats_packages()) |>
  setdiff(rownames(installed.packages(priority = "base"))) |>
  c("tidyverse", "tidymodels", "easystats") |>
  sort() |>
  pak::pkg_status()
```

```{r}
pkgs |>
  summarize(
    Packages = list(unique(unlist(Packages))),
    .by = Lesson
  ) |>
  reframe(
    Lesson = glue("[{Lesson}]({Lesson}//)"),
    Packages = sapply(Packages, \(x) glue('`{x}`') |> glue_collapse(sep = ", "))
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

<details><summary><i>Installing R Packages</i></summary>

You can install all the R packages used by running:

```{r}
pak_list <- pkgs_info |>
  transmute(
    prefix = case_when(
      repotype %in% c("cran", "bioc") ~ glue("{package}"),
      remotetype == "github" ~ glue("github::{remotepkgref}")
    ),
    comma = rep(c(",", ""), c(nrow(pkgs_info) - 1, 1)),
    version = glue("# {version}")
  ) |>
  glue_data('    "{prefix}"{comma} {version}') |>
  glue_collapse(sep = "\n")

cat(
  "# in alphabetical order:",
  "",
  "pak::pak(",
  "  c(",
  pak_list,
  "  )",
  ")",
  sep = "\n"
)
```

</details>

### Python Modules


```{r}
extract_modules <- function(fl) {
  if (length(fl) == 1) {
    txt <- read.delim(fl, header = FALSE)[[1]]

    mods <- str_extract_all(
      string = txt,
      pattern = "(?<=^(import|from)\\s)[a-zA-Z0-9_]{1,}"
    )

    mods <- unlist(mods)

    dir_py_files <- dirname(fl) |>
      list.files(pattern = "\\.py$", full.names = TRUE) |>
      basename() |>
      str_remove(pattern = "\\.py$")

    mods <- setdiff(mods, dir_py_files)
  } else if (length(fl) > 1) {
    mods <- sapply(fl, extract_modules)
  }

  mods |>
    unlist(recursive = TRUE) |>
    unique()
}

py_files <- list.files(pattern = ".py$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)

py_files <- py_files[str_detect(py_files, "^\\./\\d{2}")]

py_lesson_names <- str_extract(py_files, pattern = "(?<=(/)).{1,}(?=(/))")

py_list <- split(py_files, py_lesson_names)

py_mdls <- lapply(py_list, extract_modules)

py_df <- tibble(
  Lesson = names(py_mdls),
  Modules = py_mdls
)

py_df |>
  mutate(
    Lesson = glue("[{Lesson}]({Lesson}//)"),
    Modules = sapply(Modules, \(x) glue('`{x}`') |> glue_collapse(sep = ", ")),
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

<details>
<summary><i>Installing Python Modules</i></summary>

You can install all the Python modules used by saving a `requirements.txt` file:

```{r}
# fmt: skip
reticulate::use_python(
  fs::path_home("AppData", "Local", "Programs", "Python", "Python313", "python.exe"),
  required = TRUE
)

imp <- reticulate::import("importlib.metadata")

py_version <- possibly(imp$version, otherwise = "")

py_mdls <- py_mdls |>
  unlist(recursive = TRUE) |>
  unique() |>
  sort()


py_mdl_info <- tibble(
  module = case_match(
    py_mdls,
    "sklearn" ~ "scikit-learn",
    "imblearn" ~ "imbalanced-learn",
    .default = py_mdls
  ),
  version = sapply(module, py_version)
) |>
  arrange(module)

py_mdl_info |>
  glue_data(
    "{module}{ifelse(nzchar(py_mdl_info$version), '>=', '')}{version}"
  ) |>
  glue_collapse(sep = "\n") |>
  cat()
```

And then running

```
pip install -r requirements.txt
```
